title: Backcasting Robust Honeypots: Does Misaligned Behavior Survive When the Honeypot Looks Less Like a Trap?

original_idea.body: Produce a graded series of honeypot prompts from obvious-trap to realistic and measure an open model's misaligned-action rate across the gradient to give a realism-sensitivity curve.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Realism-sensitivity informs whether deployment-time elicitation traps work.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompt-grading plus measuring misaligned-action rate; accessible to a motivated beginner.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single realism-sensitivity curve with defined success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Honeypot design is neglected, lab-independent third-party scrutiny.

novelty.reasoning: Honeypot detectability studied in 2026; graded realism curve may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Honeypot realism is an active topic; this specific gradient curve may be open.
